input.question: What kind of cells are generated in scars? Why are some different than its' original cells
input.ground_truth: The cells produced are "backup cells". They are long cells arranged parallel to each other in order to regrow as fast as possible. Unfortunately, these cells are not as strong and may not match the original tissue.

response.prediction:
Okay! Let's imagine your skin is like a big blanket.

When you get a cut, the blanket gets a hole. Your body sends special helpers called cells to fix the hole. These helpers make a new kind of blanket patch—this is called a **scar**.

The new patch (scar) is made of a different kind of cell. Instead of the soft, stretchy cells that were there before (like the soft part of the blanket), the scar is made mostly of strong, tough cells. These tough cells are called **fibroblasts**, and they make something called **collagen**. Collagen is like strong glue that helps hold the patch together.

So, the scar is made of different cells because your body wants to make something strong and quick to close the hole, not something soft and stretchy like before. That's why the scar feels different and looks different from the rest of your skin!
